book_s_hat_0.text: Milo lost his red hat in the park.

book_s_hat_1.text: Then it began to rain, so Milo felt cold.

book_s_hat_2.text: A kind duck found the hat and gave it back.

book_s_seeds_0.text: Tia planted seeds in a pot.

book_s_seeds_1.text: She gave them water every day.

book_s_seeds_2.text: After many days, a green plant came up.

bookq_s_seeds_2.text: What came up after many days?

book_s_berries_1.text: The berries were too high to reach.

book_s_berries_2.text: He stacked three logs and climbed up to eat.

bookq_s_berries_0.text: Why did Milo stack the logs?

bookq_s_berries_2.text: What kind of fox is Milo?

book_s_kite_1.text: The wind was strong, so the kite flew high.

book_s_kite_2.text: Then the string broke, and the kite floated away.

bookq_s_kite_0.text: Why did the kite fly high?

bookq_s_kite_2.text: How did Leo feel at the end?

book_s_puppy_0.text: A little puppy got lost in the rain.

book_s_puppy_1.text: A girl named Anu found him shivering under a bench.

book_s_puppy_2.text: She wrapped him in her scarf and took him home.

bookq_s_puppy_0.text: Where did Anu find the puppy?

bookq_s_puppy_2.text: What kind of girl is Anu?

book_s_rocket_0.text: Kabir built a rocket from an old box.

book_s_rocket_1.text: He painted it silver and drew stars on the side.

book_s_rocket_2.text: When his little sister saw it, she clapped and asked for a ride.

book_s_rocket_3.text: Kabir smiled and made room for two.

bookq_s_rocket_0.text: What did Kabir use to build the rocket?

bookq_s_rocket_1.text: What did he do after painting it?

bookq_s_rocket_2.text: Why did Kabir make room for two?

bookq_s_rocket_3.text: What will they probably do next?

book_s_market_0.text: Every Sunday, Meera goes to the market with her grandfather.

book_s_market_1.text: Today he forgot his bag, so Meera carried the mangoes in her skirt.

book_s_market_2.text: Grandfather laughed and called her his clever helper.

bookq_s_market_0.text: When does Meera go to the market?

bookq_s_market_1.text: Why did Meera carry mangoes in her skirt?

bookq_s_market_2.text: How did Grandfather feel about Meera?

book_s_turtle_0.text: Tortu the turtle wanted to see the sunrise from the top of the hill.

book_s_turtle_1.text: He started walking at midnight because he knew he was slow.

book_s_turtle_2.text: When the sun came up, Tortu was sitting at the top, smiling.

bookq_s_turtle_0.text: Why did Tortu start walking at midnight?

bookq_s_turtle_1.text: Where was Tortu when the sun came up?

book_s_library_0.text: Zoya loved the library because it was calm.

book_s_library_1.text: One day a bird flew in through the window and began to sing.

book_s_library_2.text: Everyone looked up from their books.

book_s_library_3.text: The librarian opened the window wide, and the bird flew back to its tree.

bookq_s_library_0.text: Why did Zoya love the library?

bookq_s_library_1.text: What happened after the bird began to sing?

bookq_s_library_2.text: Why did the librarian open the window wide?

book_s_rain_0.text: The farmers in the village waited for rain for many weeks.

book_s_rain_1.text: The fields were dry and the cows were thirsty.

book_s_rain_2.text: One evening dark clouds rolled in, and big drops began to fall.

book_s_rain_3.text: The children ran outside and danced in the puddles.

bookq_s_rain_1.text: What happened just before the drops began to fall?

bookq_s_rain_2.text: How did the children feel when it rained?

bookq_s_rain_3.text: What will the fields look like in a few weeks?

book_s_robot_0.text: Bolt the robot could carry heavy boxes and fix broken clocks, but he had never had a friend.

book_s_robot_1.text: One day a little girl dropped her ice cream and started to cry.

book_s_robot_2.text: Bolt could not fix ice cream, so he simply sat beside her and offered his hand.

bookq_s_robot_1.text: Why did the girl start to cry?

book_s_island_0.text: While walking on the beach, Arjun found a glass bottle with a rolled-up note inside.

book_s_island_1.text: The note said, “Whoever finds this, please write back.

book_s_island_2.text: I live on the island across the sea.”

book_s_island_3.text: Arjun ran home, found his best pencil, and began writing a long letter about his town.

bookq_s_island_0.text: Where did Arjun find the bottle?

bookq_s_island_2.text: What is the person who wrote the note probably feeling?

bookq_s_island_3.text: What will Arjun most likely do with his letter?

book_s_festival_0.text: The night before the lantern festival, a storm tore Arya’s lantern into pieces.

book_s_festival_1.text: Instead of crying, she collected the torn paper and made five tiny lanterns.

book_s_festival_2.text: At the festival, she gave them to children who had none.

book_s_festival_3.text: The sky that night had more lights than ever before.

bookq_s_festival_1.text: What did Arya do with the torn paper?

bookq_s_festival_2.text: Why were there more lights than ever before?

book_s_cloud_0.text: Far above the islands lived a small grey cloud named Gumsum.

book_s_cloud_1.text: Every evening he watched families reading together, but no one ever looked up at him.

book_s_cloud_2.text: One night a girl noticed him, smiled, and read her favourite book out loud to the sky.

book_s_cloud_3.text: Gumsum listened so carefully that he forgot to rain.

bookq_s_cloud_0.text: What did Gumsum watch every evening?

bookq_s_cloud_1.text: Why did Gumsum forget to rain?

bookq_s_cloud_2.text: How had Gumsum felt before that night?

bookq_s_cloud_3.text: What might Gumsum do the next evening?
